title: When the Ember Wakes
premise: Silas Galloway, a bone-carver in the godless valley of Hollowmere, has always heard the dead through the bones he carves—a gift the valley's ancient wards were meant to suppress, not create. When prayers begin landing on his workbench instead of reaching the old gods, Silas realizes the gods aren't returning: they're dead, and something is wearing their voices to lure worshippers into feeding it. Hunted by the Ashen Order, who enforce the valley's exile, and guided by a found family of outcasts—a disgraced order knight, a runaway prayer-scribe, and a ghost with no name—Silas must decide whether to destroy the false gods' vessel or claim its power. In the end, Silas shatters the vessel and gives their own voice to the dead, becoming the valley's first honest god while choosing to remain human, mortal, and home.
about_author: T. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist turned novelist who writes about grief, small towns, and the stubborn persistence of the forgotten. They live at the edge of a forest that may or may not be listening.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Silas Galloway carves a memorial femur for a drowned child and hears her last words—impossible, since magic cannot cross Hollowmere's borders. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine; the first crack in a lifetime of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Prayers on the Workbench
chapters.summary: Written prayers begin appearing physically among Silas's bone shavings, addressed to gods the valley forbids naming. A stranger, the runaway scribe Wren, arrives asking who has been answering them. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a thrilling sense of being needed for the first time.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Knelt
chapters.summary: An Ashen Order knight, Ser Odile Vane, arrives hunting 'heresy,' but Silas recognizes her as the woman who once wept over a grave he carved. She covers for him—for now. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: divided loyalty; duty grinding against memory.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Silas carves an ancient relic bone from the valley's edge and hears a chorus of gods screaming—not returning, but dying, long ago. The wards didn't keep magic out; they kept the murder scene sealed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything Silas believed about home.

chapters.title: A Ghost With No Name
chapters.summary: A nameless ghost begins following Wren, able to speak only through borrowed mouths. It warns that something is 'wearing the voices.' The three form a wary pact. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: loneliness finding its first fragile family.

chapters.title: The Order's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile discovers the Ashen Order has known the gods died for centuries and has been harvesting worship to feed something in the deep vaults. She burns her orders—or tries to. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Market Day Fire
chapters.summary: A possessed pilgrim ignites the market, speaking in a chorus of divine voices. Silas saves children using bone-hearing to find them through smoke, exposing their gift publicly. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: heroism at the cost of anonymity—the valley now watches them.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Oldest Law
chapters.summary: The valley council demands Silas submit to warding or exile. Wren argues flight; Odile argues truth; Silas refuses both, insisting the valley deserves to know it was built on a massacre. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: defiance born of love for a place that would erase them.

chapters.title: The Deep Vault
chapters.summary: Guided by the nameless ghost, the trio infiltrates the Order's vault and finds the vessel: a fused mass of stolen god-bones, half-awake, whispering Silas's name. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion; the enemy is made of everything holy.

chapters.title: Voices in the Dark
chapters.summary: Trapped in the vault, each character hears their deepest shame spoken aloud in a loved one's voice. Wren nearly walks into the vessel; Silas pulls them back by singing a real, living voice. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror overcome by chosen family.

chapters.title: Exile
chapters.summary: The council brands Silas a witch; Odile is stripped of rank for defending them. The trio flees across the wardline—and magic floods back into Silas like blood into a numb limb. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loss transformed into terrifying new power.

chapters.title: The God-Road
chapters.summary: Outside the valley, the land is scarred with the old war's ruins. The ghost recovers fragments of its name: it was the youngest god, the one who survived by hiding inside a human line—Silas's line. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by inheritance no one asked for.

chapters.title: Ashen Camp
chapters.summary: Captured by Order remnants, the group learns High Custodian Marrow plans to fully wake the vessel and rule as its sole interpreter. Odile confronts her former mentor and loses badly. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Fragments of the true dead gods, scattered in roadside shrines, offer Silas their remaining strength—if Silas will carry them, body and bone. Accepting means never being only human again. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation weighed against identity.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren admits they were the Order's scribe who transcribed the prayers that fed the vessel—they led pilgrims to it unknowingly. The group forgives unevenly, painfully, honestly. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt met not with absolution but with belonging anyway.

chapters.title: March of the Faithful
chapters.summary: Marrow leads thousands of desperate worshippers toward Hollowmere to wake the vessel at the site of the gods' murder. The trio races ahead through a storm of answered prayers gone wrong. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grim urgency; ordinary people weaponized by hope.

chapters.title: The Wardline Breaks
chapters.summary: Marrow shatters the valley's wards; Hollowmere's generations-long silence ends in a single deafening instant. Every dead voice in the valley speaks at once—and Silas alone can hear them all. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: overwhelming grief becoming clarity.

chapters.title: What We Buried Alive
chapters.summary: In the vault, the full truth surfaces: the founders killed the gods to steal their power and built the valley's peace on the theft. The council kneels or flees. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by sorrow for complicity.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: Marrow wakes the vessel; it rises wearing every dead god's face and offers Silas godhood to stand aside. Silas refuses—not out of virtue, but because they refuse to become another thing people pray to instead of talk to. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the climax's moral heart.

chapters.title: Emberfall
chapters.summary: Battle in the bone-vault: Odile holds the door at terrible cost, Wren unbinds the stolen prayers, and Silas sings the true names of the murdered gods into the vessel until it remembers what it ate—and grieves itself apart. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: cathartic, costly victory.

chapters.title: The Honest God
chapters.summary: The freed god-fragments ask Silas to be their vessel permanently. Silas instead teaches the valley to hear its own dead—carving listening-bones for every household—and keeps only a single ember of divinity, shared rather than held. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: humility as triumph.

chapters.title: When the Ember Wakes
chapters.summary: Seasons later, Hollowmere holds its first honest funeral in three hundred years. Odile rebuilds the Order as guardians of memory, Wren writes prayers that expect no answer, and the nameless ghost finally rests, named. Silas carves, listens, stays. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—an ending that chooses home over power.
